title: Do S&P500 Options Increase Market Volatility? Evidence from 0DTEs
one_line: 0DTE options did not raise S&P 500 volatility — index volatility was ~60 bps (annualized) lower on 0DTE days; dealers are net LONG gamma on expiration days, which predicts lower 10-minute volatility and stronger short-term reversal in E-mini order flow.

findings.statement: Index volatility ≈ 60 bps annualized lower on days with 0DTE trading (before daily expiries, May 2022).
Each 1 bp rise in hedging needs ≈ 4 bp lower realized volatility.

Dealers net long gamma on expiration days; higher net gamma predicts lower volatility over ~10 minutes (fades within an hour), stronger E-mini order-flow reversals and negative high-frequency momentum.

why.pattern: Execution mechanics: long-gamma dealer hedging dampens moves and produces short-term reversal.
why.mechanism: Dealers holding positive gamma sell into rallies and buy dips while hedging.

reported_results.headline: 0DTE dampens volatility; long dealer gamma → short-term reversal.

tradable_edge: Context: since 2022 the close and intraday may be more mean-reverting; every momentum spec must report pre/post 2022 separately.
angles: Pre/post May 2022 split in all intraday momentum tests
data_fit: ES 1-min Dec 2013 → Sep 2026, NQ 1-min Jul 2021 → Sep 2026 (2024+ protected in the backtest project).
